purpose: Precisely specified observable strategy candidates for prospective evaluation; the feature audit is independent of candidate performance.

audit.waste_history_assumption: For draw-one, every buried waste card was previously exposed. The three waste-unlock features can be computed with perfect memory or permitted waste inspection. They are not functions of the currently exposed waste card alone. For draw-three, buried packet cards need not previously have been exposed, so this exemption does not automatically apply.
audit.first_empty_with_king: A first empty column can only be created by removing an entire tableau source. That move exposes no unknown card; its successor king availability is computable from visible cards.
audit.empty_king_queen_access: Excluded: moving a king-led stack into an empty column can uncover an unknown source queen, which changes the successor queen count.
audit.unknown_stock_conservatism: All stock identities are treated as unknown, including recycled cards a perfect-memory player might remember. Thus candidate policies do not rely on stock memory.
audit.validation_scope: Unit tests permute hidden tableau and stock identities while preserving the visible position, and check audited features and candidate greedy choices. This tests Python move features; it is not a proof of every native evaluation or of human learnability.

evaluation_contract.scoring: For each eligible legal move, sum weight times feature value and select the highest score.
evaluation_contract.tie_break: First generated eligible move wins a tie. Order: draw/recycle; waste-to-foundation; waste-to-tableau by destination; then each tableau source left-to-right, foundation move first, transfers with longer stacks first and destinations left-to-right.
evaluation_contract.history: Existing Python/native evaluators reject successor positions previously seen in the same game, with exact full-state memory. This must be stated with any measured win rate; finite tests below check observation invariance on a coupled short history, not the full-state-memory assumption in general.
evaluation_contract.native_pruning: Native additionally drops whole-pile transfers into an empty column and retains only the first equivalent empty destination. Python legal_moves lists these options. Existing n=2 parity evidence does not prove parity for every strategy or n=13.

candidates.name: rounded_3
candidates.label: Three-term score
candidates.information_model: current visible cards, tableau/stock/waste sizes, foundations, and pass count; no buried-waste memory needed
explanation: Add 10 for a safe foundation move.
Add 5 if the move uncovers a face-down tableau card.
Subtract 1 per card placed onto the tableau.
candidates.provenance: Manual rounded score proposed from stage7 fitted weights and feature ablations. Not retuned or evaluated; no performance claim.

candidates.name: rounded_5
candidates.label: Five-term score
candidates.information_model: current visible cards, tableau/stock/waste sizes, foundations, and pass count; no buried-waste memory needed
explanation: Add 1 for playing the waste card onto the tableau.
candidates.provenance: Manual rounded score proposed from stage7 fitted weights and feature ablations. Not retuned or evaluated; no performance claim.

candidates.name: rounded_8
candidates.label: Eight-term score
candidates.information_model: current visible cards, tableau/stock/waste sizes, foundations, and pass count; no buried-waste memory needed
explanation: For a revealing move, add the number of face-down cards in its source before the move.
For a tableau transfer that reveals a face-down card or empties its source, add 0.75 per card moved (partially offsets the tableau penalty).
candidates.provenance: Manual rounded score proposed from stage7 fitted weights and feature ablations. Not retuned or evaluated; no performance claim.
